login.note: Substack prefers a passwordless emailed magic link ('Sign in with email'); there is also a password form behind 'Sign in with password', plus Google/Apple/Twitter buttons. The magic-link flow means the human needs the mailbox open in another window, and the link opens a NEW tab which is where the session actually lands.

logout.note: Sign-out is reachable from the account menu; the session cookies (connect.sid / substack.sid) are HttpOnly, so clearing them from JS is not possible. A publication subdomain shares the login but is a separate origin — check substack.com itself after signing out.

traps: GET /api/v1/subscriptions answers HTTP 401 with a JSON BODY when signed out — {"errors":[{"msg":"Please sign in", "msgHTML":"Please sign in."}]} (verified 2026-09-12). It is valid JSON and it parses cleanly, so any check of the shape 'the fetch resolved and the body parsed' calls a signed-out session live. Read the status, then read the field.

window._preloads.userSettings exists on the signed-out page with user_id: null (verified 2026-09-12 on both substack.com/ and a publication subdomain). The key's presence is not the answer, its value is.

substack.com/home 302-redirects to / when signed out (verified 2026-09-12) — not a 401, not a 404. A fetch that follows redirects lands on a 200 marketing page, which is exactly what 'it worked' looks like.

Every publication is its own origin: <pub>.substack.com serves its own _preloads and its own /api/v1/*. A relative API fetch made from a publication page hits the publication host, not substack.com, and the two do not return the same user-scoped data. Probe on substack.com.

In the HTML, _preloads is assigned as window._preloads = JSON.parse("...") — a JSON string inside a JSON string, so anything scraping the markup must unescape twice (this is what yt-dlp's extractor does). In a live page it is already an object; the probe handles both.

Neither /api/v1/user nor /api/v1/profile exists on substack.com: both answer 404 with an HTML page, not a JSON error (verified 2026-09-12). Guessing a REST-looking who-am-I path here gets an HTML body and a confident wrong answer.
notes: PROBE STRATEGY: (b) a credentialed same-origin fetch of a session-gated endpoint, corroborated by (a) the page's own state object. Both halves were checked against live signed-out responses on 2026-09-12: GET /api/v1/subscriptions returns 401 {"errors":[{"msg":"Please sign in"}]} with no session, and window._preloads.userSettings.user_id is null on a signed-out document. The probe reads _preloads first (free, no request), then fetches /api/v1/subscriptions: 401/403 is a signed-out verdict, and a 200 must still carry a user object (or a non-null _preloads user_id) before it counts — a bare 200 is explicitly not enough. The signed-in shape of that body was NOT observed (no session was available), so the probe accepts j.user / j.currentUser / subscriptions[0].user and falls back to the _preloads id; that fallback is the part most likely to need adjusting on first live verification. The session cookies are HttpOnly, so document.cookie is never consulted. WHAT A READ RECIPE SHOULD DO: read the internal JSON API rather than the DOM, on the right origin. For the signed-in reader surface, /api/v1/subscriptions is the list of what this account follows, and the Notes surface is under /api/v1/notes; both need the session cookie and are same-origin on substack.com. For any publication, the stable and well-worn path is https://<pub>.substack.com/api/v1/archive?sort=new&limit=12&offset=0 for the post list and /api/v1/posts/<slug> for one post, neither of which needs a session for free content. For a single rendered page, window._preloads.post / _preloads.pub carries the whole post object already parsed. Paywalled bodies require the session and are the one place a read genuinely depends on auth. WRITE: empty — no publish path here has been observed, and Substack's write endpoints (notes, comments, drafts) all carry CSRF material minted in the page that no verb here captures yet.

Signed-OUT path proven again; signed-IN path still a hypothesis (profile is not signed in here).
